nodes.name: Measurement loop over the shared copies
nodes.statement: \textbf{For} $i=1$ to $\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil$, \begin{enumerate} \item Alice performs the measurement $\set{P_A,I_A- P_A}$ on each register $A_1^iA^i_2$ where, \begin{equation} P_A\defeq\sum_i\ket{a_i}_{A_1}\bra{a_i}_{A_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m}_{A_2}\bra{m}_{A_2}\right) . \end{equation} On each index $i$, she declares \textit{success} if her outcome corresponds to $P_A$. \item Bob performs the measurement $\set{P_B,I_B- P_B}$ on each register $B_1^iB^i_2$ where, \begin{equation} P_B\defeq \sum_i\ket{b_i}_{B_1}\bra{b_i}_{B_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{\min\{\frac{K}{\delta} 2^{c'} b_i,K\}}\ket{m}_{B_2}\bra{m}_{B_2}\right) . \end{equation} On each index $i$, he declares \textit{success} if his outcome corresponds to $P_B$. \end{enumerate} \textbf{Endfor}
nodes.statement_short: Loop over all $\lceil N\log(1/\delta)\rceil$ shared copies; Alice measures $\{P_A,I-P_A\}$ and Bob measures $\{P_B,I-P_B\}$, each recording successes.

nodes.name: Abort if Alice never succeeds
nodes.statement: If Alice does not succeed on any index, she aborts.
nodes.statement_short: Abort when Alice has no successful index.

nodes.name: Alice sends the block index
nodes.statement: Else, Alice selects the first index $m$ where she succeeds and sends to Bob the binary encoding of $k=\lceil m/N\rceil$ using $\lceil\log\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil$ bits.
nodes.statement_short: Alice sends the block index $k=\lceil m/N\rceil$ of her first success.

nodes.name: Alice sends hash values
nodes.statement: Alice sends $\{ h_l(m\mod N) |~ l \in [\lceil r + 2\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil]\}$ to Bob.
nodes.statement_short: Alice sends $\lceil r+2\log(1/\delta)\rceil$ shared hash values of her index.

nodes.name: Bob matches hashes and outputs
nodes.statement: Define $S_B \defeq \{ t |~ \text{ Bob succeeds on index } $t$\} \cap \{(k-1)N, \cdots, k N -1\}$. If $S_B$ is empty, he outputs $\ketbra{0}$. Bob selects the first index $n$ in $S_B$ such that $\forall l \in [\lceil r + 2\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil]: h_l(n \mod N) = h_l(m \mod N) $ and outputs the state in $B_1^n$ (if no such index exists, he outputs $\ketbra{0}$).
nodes.statement_short: Bob outputs the register of his first successful index in the announced block whose hashes match Alice's.

nodes.name: Share public coins and entanglement
nodes.statement: Alice and Bob share public coins according to distribution $\rho_{D_{-j}U_{-j}}$, and the shared entanglement needed to run the protocol $\P$ from Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol}.
nodes.statement_short: Sample the public coins $d_{-j}u_{-j}$ and set up the entanglement needed for Theorem 3.1.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Embed the input in coordinate $j$
nodes.statement: Alice and Bob are given the input $(x,y)\sim\mu$. They embed the input to the $j$-th coordinate $X_jY_j$. The input is independent of shared randomness, from equation (\ref{eqn:directsumpubliccoins}).
nodes.statement_short: Place the single input $(x,y)$ into the $j$-th coordinate of the $k$-fold protocol.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Each party computes its conditional state
nodes.statement: Given input $(x_j,y_j)\equiv (x,y)$ and shared public coins $d_{-j}u_{-j}$, Alice knows the eigen-decomposition of the state $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, since $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}=\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$. Bob knows the eigen-decomposition of state $\rho_{B}^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Alice computes the message state conditioned on her input; Bob computes his own conditional state.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Run the compression protocol
nodes.statement: They run the protocol in Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol} with inputs $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Alice) and $\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Bob). After communicating $\mathcal{O}(4c/\delta^9)$ bits to Bob, Bob receives a state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfying $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ if $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\in G$.
nodes.statement_short: Run Theorem 3.1 with parameter $4c/\delta$ so Bob receives a state $\delta$-close in $\ell_1$.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Bob samples the remaining inputs
nodes.statement: Bob samples the distribution from $\rho_{Y_{-j}}$, since he has the registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$. This is possible from equation \ref{eqn:dumarkov}, which states that register $Y_{-j}$ is independent of registers $A,B,X$ conditioned on registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$.
nodes.statement_short: Bob samples $Y_{-j}$ locally, which is legitimate by the Markov condition.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Bob decodes and outputs
nodes.statement: Bob applies the unitary $V$, as in the protocol $\Q$, on registers $BY\equiv E_BMY$ and then measures the register $Z$. He outputs the outcome.
nodes.statement_short: Bob applies the original decoder $V$ and measures the answer register.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Alice rejection-samples her spectrum
nodes.statement: For each $i>0$, Alice performs the measurement $\set{P_A,I- P_A}$ on the registers $A^i_1A^i_2$, where \begin{equation*} P_A\defeq\sum_i\ket{a_i}_{A_1}\bra{a_i}_{A_1}\otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m}_{A_2}\bra{m}_{A_2}\right) \end{equation*} She declares \textit{success} if she obtains outcome corresponding to $P_A$. She stops once she succeeds in some register $A^j$, and swaps $A^j$ with $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Alice measures $\{P_A,I-P_A\}$ on successive copies and swaps her first success into the output register.

nodes.name: Bob rejection-samples his spectrum
nodes.statement: For each $i>0$, Bob performs the measurement $\set{P_B,I- P_B}$ on the registers $B^i_1B^i_2$, where \begin{equation*} P_B\defeq\sum_i\ket{b_i}_{B_1}\bra{b_i}_{B_1}\otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{Kb_i}\ket{m}_{B_2}\bra{m}_{B_2}\right) \end{equation*} He declares \textit{success} if he obtains outcome corresponding to $P_B$. He stops once he succeeds in some register $B^j$, and swaps $B^j$ with $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Bob measures $\{P_B,I-P_B\}$ on successive copies and swaps his first success into the output register.

nodes.name: Purify and project
nodes.statement: Introduce a register $B$, such that $|B|\geq |A|$. Let $\phi\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$ be a purification of $\rho$. Then $( \Pi \otimes I_B)\phi ( \Pi \otimes I_B)$ is a purification of $\Pi \rho \Pi $.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce a purification $\phi$ of $\rho$; the projected vector purifies $\Pi\rho\Pi$.

nodes.name: Apply monotonicity of fidelity
nodes.statement: Hence (using monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation, Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}) \[\F(\rho, \frac{\Pi \rho \Pi}{\Tr \Pi \rho } )\F\br{\phi,(\Pi\otimes I_B)\phi(\Pi\otimes I_B)}= \frac{\abs{\bra{\phi}(\Pi \otimes I) \ket{\phi}}}{\norm{(\Pi \otimes I) \ket{\phi}}} = \sqrt{\Tr( \Pi \rho)}. \myqedhere \]
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of fidelity under partial trace turns the pure-state overlap into $\sqrt{\Tr\Pi\rho}$.

nodes.name: Expand one register at a time
nodes.statement: Consider, \begin{eqnarray*} \condmutinf{A_1A_2\ldots A_k}{B}{C}_{\rho}&=&\condmutinf{A_1}{B}{C}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{A_2A_3\ldots A_k}{B}{A_1C}_\rho\\ &=&\condmutinf{A_1}{B}{C}_{\rho}+\mutinf{A_2A_3\ldots A_k}{A_1BC}_{\rho}-\mutinf{A_1}{A_2A_3\ldots A_k}\rho\\ &=&\condmutinf{A_1}{B}{C}_{\rho}+\mutinf{A_2A_3\ldots A_k}{A_1BC}_{\rho}\\ &\geq&\condmutinf{A_1}{B}{C}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{A_2A_3\ldots A_k}{B}{C}_{\rho} \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain-rule expansion peeling off $A_1$ and dropping the independent mutual-information term.

nodes.name: Justify the steps and induct
nodes.statement: The first and second equalities follow from the definition of the conditional mutual information. The third equality is from the independence between $A_1$ and $A_2A_3\ldots A_k$. The last inequality is from strong subadditivity (Fact~\ref{fact:strongsubadditivity}). Proof follows by induction.
nodes.statement_short: Justify each equality and close the argument by induction on the number of registers.

nodes.name: Introduce the classical distributions $R$, $R'$
nodes.statement: Define $R_{ij}\defeq a_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{g_j}}^2$ and $R'_{ij}\defeq g_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{g_j}}^2$. Note that both $R \defeq \{R_{ij}\}$ and $R' \defeq \{R'_{ij}\}$ form probability distributions over $[N^2]$. Also note that $\F(R,R') = \Tr(\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\rho'})$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $R,R'$ on $[N^2]$ and note $\F(R,R')=\Tr(\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\rho'})$.

nodes.name: Chain of inequalities for the overlap
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the overlap as $\sum\min(R,R')$ and bound it through fidelity and $\ell_1$ inequalities.

nodes.name: Justify each step
nodes.statement: where the first equality is from the definitions of $\ket{S_A(\rho)}$ and $\ket{S_A(\rho')}$; the second equality is from the definition of $\ell_1$ distance; the first inequality is from ~\ref{fact:tracefidelityequi}; the second inequality is from the fact that $\Tr\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\rho'}\leq 1$; the third inequality is from Facts~\ref{fact:fidelityvstrace}.
nodes.statement_short: Attribute each equality and inequality to the relevant definition or fact.

nodes.name: Compute $(I_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S_A(\rho')}$
nodes.statement: Consider, \begin{equation*} (I_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S_A(\rho')} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_{i,j=1}^N\ket{\conjugate{g_j}} \ket{b_i}\braket{b_i}{g_j} \left(\sum_{m=1}^{\min\{\lceil Kg_j\rceil, \frac{K}{\delta} 2^{c'}b_i\}}\ket{m, m} \right). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand Bob's projector acting on the $\rho'$ sampling state.

nodes.name: Lower-bound the norm using Claim 3.3
nodes.statement: Therefore, \begin{align} & \norm{(I_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S_A(\rho')} }^2 \geq \sum_{i,j=1}^N \abs{\braket{b_i}{g_j}}^2 \min\{g_j, \frac{1}{\delta}2^{c'}b_i \} \nonumber \\ & \geq \sum_{j=1}^N g_j \left(\sum_{i|~b_i\geq \delta 2^{-c'}g_j} \abs{\braket{b_i}{g_j}}^2 \right) \geq \sum_{j=1}^N g_j(1- \delta) = 1- \delta . \quad \mbox{(using Claim~\ref{claim:1})} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Claim 3.3 gives $\norm{(I_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S_A(\rho')}}^2\geq 1-\delta$.

nodes.name: Transfer the bound from $\rho'$ to $\rho$
nodes.statement: Using the above, \begin{align*} & \prob{\text{Bob succeeds}|~\text{Alice succeeds}} = \Tr (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)} \\ & \geq \Tr (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho')} - \frac{1}{2} \onenorm{S_A(\rho) - S_A(\rho')} \\ & = \Tr (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho')} - \sqrt{1- \abs{\braket{S_A(\rho)}{S_A(\rho')}}^2} \quad \mbox{(Fact~\ref{fact:tracefidelityequi})} \\ & \geq 1 - \delta - 2 \sqrt{ (1-\F(\rho,\rho'))^{1/2}} . \quad \mbox{(Claim~\ref{claim:2} and Eq.~\eqref{eq:probonrho'})} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Pay the $\ell_1$ distance between the two sampling states, controlled by Claim 3.4.

nodes.name: Apply the gentle measurement lemma
nodes.statement: From gentle measurement lemma (Fact~\ref{fact:gentlemeasurement}), $$\F(S_A(\rho), \frac{(I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)} (I_A\otimes P_B) }{\Tr (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)}}) \geq \sqrt{\Tr (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Bob's successful projection barely disturbs $\ket{S_A(\rho)}$.

nodes.name: Push the bound through the partial trace
nodes.statement: Since the marginal of $\ket{S_A(\rho)}$ on register $B$ is $\rho$ and partial trace does not decrease fidelity (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}), using item 2. above, the desired result follows.
nodes.statement_short: The marginal on $B$ is $\rho$ and partial trace does not decrease fidelity.

nodes.name: Bound $\prob{T_1}$
nodes.statement: \item $\prob{T_1}\leq\br{1-\frac{1}{N}}^{\lceil N \cdot \log\frac{1}{\ve}\rceil}\leq \exp^{-\lceil\log\frac{1}{\ve}\rceil}\leq \delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Independent repetitions make the probability that Alice never succeeds at most $\delta$.

nodes.name: Bound $\prob{T_2}$
nodes.statement: Follows from Claim \ref{claim:relativeprob}. \item For this argument we condition on $\neg T_1$ for all events below. From Claim \ref{claim:successprob} and the fact that Bob independently measures each index, we have $\expec{}{\abs{S_B}}= N\cdot \prob{\text{Bob succeeds}} \leq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta}$. Using Markov's inequality, \begin{equation} \prob{\abs{S_B} \geq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve}}\leq \frac{\delta\ve}{2^{c'}} \cdot \expec{}{\abs{S_B}} \leq \ve . \end{equation} Thus \begin{align*} \prob{T_3} & \leq\prob{\abs{S_B}\geq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve} \text{ or } m \notin S_B} + \prob{T_3~|~m \in S_B \text{ and } \abs{S_B}\leq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve}} \\ & \leq \prob{\abs{S_B}\geq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve}} + \prob{T_2} + \prob{T_3~|~m \in S_B \text{ and } \abs{S_B}\leq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve}} \\ & \leq 2 \ve+\prob{T_3~|~m \in S_B \text{ and } \abs{S_B}\leq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve}} \quad \mbox{(Eq.~\eqref{eq:sb} and item 2. of this claim)}\\ & \leq 2\ve + 2^{- \lceil c' + \log\frac{1}{\delta}+ 2\log\frac{1}{\ve}\rceil} \cdot \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve} \quad \leq \quad 3 \ve. \end{align*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Claim 3.5 already bounds the probability that Bob misses Alice's index.

nodes.name: Bound $\prob{T_3}$
nodes.statement: For this argument we condition on $\neg T_1$ for all events below. From Claim \ref{claim:successprob} and the fact that Bob independently measures each index, we have $\expec{}{\abs{S_B}}= N\cdot \prob{\text{Bob succeeds}} \leq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta}$. Using Markov's inequality, \begin{equation} \prob{\abs{S_B} \geq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve}}\leq \frac{\delta\ve}{2^{c'}} \cdot \expec{}{\abs{S_B}} \leq \ve . \end{equation} Thus \begin{align*} \prob{T_3} & \leq\prob{\abs{S_B}\geq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve} \text{ or } m \notin S_B} + \prob{T_3~|~m \in S_B \text{ and } \abs{S_B}\leq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve}} \\ & \leq \prob{\abs{S_B}\geq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve}} + \prob{T_2} + \prob{T_3~|~m \in S_B \text{ and } \abs{S_B}\leq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve}} \\ & \leq 2 \ve+\prob{T_3~|~m \in S_B \text{ and } \abs{S_B}\leq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve}} \quad \mbox{(Eq.~\eqref{eq:sb} and item 2. of this claim)}\\ & \leq 2\ve + 2^{- \lceil c' + \log\frac{1}{\delta}+ 2\log\frac{1}{\ve}\rceil} \cdot \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta\ve} \quad \leq \quad 3 \ve. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Markov's inequality caps $\abs{S_B}$, and the hash values then make a wrong index unlikely.

nodes.name: Set up eigen-decompositions and parameters
nodes.statement: Let the eigen-decomposition of $\rho$ be $\sum_{i=1}^Na_i\ketbra{a_i}$ and that of $\sigma$ be $\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i\ketbra{b_i}$. Define $c\defeq\relent{\rho}{\sigma}$, $\delta \defeq (\ve/3)^4$ and $c' \defeq (c+2)/\delta$. Without loss of generality, assume $a_1,a_2\ldots a_N, \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta}b_1,\frac{2^{c'}}{\delta}b_2\ldots \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta}b_N$ to be rational numbers, and define $K$ be the least common multiple of their denominators. The error due to this assumption can be made arbitrarily close to $0$, for large enough $K$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix eigen-decompositions and the constants $c$, $\delta$, $c'$ and the common denominator $K$.

nodes.name: Introduce the registers
nodes.statement: Let $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{N}}$ be an orthonormal basis for $\H$. Introduce registers $A_1,B_1$ associated to $\H$ and registers $A_2,B_2$ associated to some Hilbert space $\H'$ with an orthonormal basis $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{K}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce registers $A_1,B_1$ on $\H$ and $A_2,B_2$ on the $K$-dimensional space $\H'$.

nodes.name: Define the shared state
nodes.statement: Consider the following state on $A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2$. \begin{equation} \ket{S}_{A_1A_2B_1B_2} \defeq \frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i=1}^N \ket{i,i}_{A_1B_1} \otimes \left( \sum_{m=1}^{K}\ket{m, m}_{A_2B_2} \right) \end{equation} For brevity, define registers $A,B$ such that $A\defeq A_1A_2$ and $B\defeq B_1B_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the maximally entangled sampling state $\ket{S}$ and abbreviate $A=A_1A_2$, $B=B_1B_2$.

nodes.name: State the protocol
nodes.statement: The protocol is described below. \begin{mdframed} \bigskip \textbf{Input:} Alice is given $\rho=\sum_{i=1}^Na_i\ketbra{a_i}$. Bob is given $\sigma=\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i\ketbra{b_i}$. \bigskip \textbf{Shared resources:} Alice and Bob hold $\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil$ registers $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ ($i \in [\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil]$), such that $A_1^i\equiv A_1, A^i_2\equiv A_2, B_1^i\equiv B_1,B_2^i\equiv B_2$. The shared state in register $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ is $\ket{S}_{A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i}$. Let $i$ refer to the `index' of corresponding registers. They also share infinitely many random hash functions $h_1,h_2,\cdots$, where each $h_l:\set{0,\cdots,N-1}\rightarrow\set{0,1}$. \begin{enumerate} \item \textbf{For} $i=1$ to $\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil$, \begin{enumerate} \item Alice performs the measurement $\set{P_A,I_A- P_A}$ on each register $A_1^iA^i_2$ where, \begin{equation} P_A\defeq\sum_i\ket{a_i}_{A_1}\bra{a_i}_{A_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m}_{A_2}\bra{m}_{A_2}\right) . \end{equation} On each index $i$, she declares \textit{success} if her outcome corresponds to $P_A$. \item Bob performs the measurement $\set{P_B,I_B- P_B}$ on each register $B_1^iB^i_2$ where, \begin{equation} P_B\defeq \sum_i\ket{b_i}_{B_1}\bra{b_i}_{B_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{\min\{\frac{K}{\delta} 2^{c'} b_i,K\}}\ket{m}_{B_2}\bra{m}_{B_2}\right) . \end{equation} On each index $i$, he declares \textit{success} if his outcome corresponds to $P_B$. \end{enumerate} \textbf{Endfor} \item If Alice does not succeed on any index, she aborts. \item Else, Alice selects the first index $m$ where she succeeds and sends to Bob the binary encoding of $k=\lceil m/N\rceil$ using $\lceil\log\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil$ bits. \item Alice sends $\{ h_l(m\mod N) |~ l \in [\lceil r + 2\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil]\}$ to Bob. \item Define $S_B \defeq \{ t |~ \text{ Bob succeeds on index } $t$\} \cap \{(k-1)N, \cdots, k N -1\}$. If $S_B$ is empty, he outputs $\ketbra{0}$. Bob selects the first index $n$ in $S_B$ such that $\forall l \in [\lceil r + 2\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil]: h_l(n \mod N) = h_l(m \mod N) $ and outputs the state in $B_1^n$ (if no such index exists, he outputs $\ketbra{0}$). \end{enumerate} \end{mdframed}
nodes.statement_short: Present the rejection-sampling plus hashing protocol that realizes the theorem.

nodes.name: Outline the analysis
nodes.statement: We analyze the protocol through a series of claims. Following claim computes the probability of success for Alice and Bob.
nodes.statement_short: Announce that the analysis proceeds through a sequence of claims, starting with the success probabilities.

nodes.name: Replace $\rho$ by a nearby $\rho'$
nodes.statement: From quantum substrate theorem (Fact \ref{fact:substrate}), there exists a state $\rho'$ which satisfies $\F(\rho,\rho')\geq 1-\delta$ and $$\rminent{\rho'}{\sigma}\leq\frac{\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+1}{\delta}+\log\frac{1}{1-\delta}\leq \frac{\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+2}{\delta}=c'.$$ We prove the following claim which is of independent interest as well.
nodes.statement_short: The substate theorem supplies $\rho'$ close to $\rho$ with $\rminent{\rho'}{\sigma}\leq c'$.

nodes.name: Define the sampling states
nodes.statement: Define $$\ket{S_A(\rho)}\defeq \frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_{i=1}^N\ket{a_i}\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m, m}\right) ; $$ $$\ket{S_A(\rho')}\defeq\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_{i=1}^N\ket{g_i}\ket{\conjugate{g_i}}\otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{\lceil Kg_i \rceil}\ket{m, m} \right) .$$ Here $\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}$ (similarly $\ket{\conjugate{g_i}}$) is the state obtained by taking complex conjugate of $\ket{a_i}$ ($\ket{g_i}$), with respect to the basis $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{N}}$ in $\H$. The following claim asserts that $\ket{S_A(\rho)}$ and $\ket{S_A(\rho')}$ are close if $\rho$ and $\rho'$ are close.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $\ket{S_A(\rho)}$ and $\ket{S_A(\rho')}$, the post-success states for the two inputs.

nodes.name: State the output-fidelity claim
nodes.statement: Finally, we show that if Alice and Bob succeed together on an index, the state in register $B$ with Bob is close to $\rho$.
nodes.statement_short: Announce the claim that joint success leaves Bob's register close to $\rho$.

nodes.name: Name the index variables
nodes.statement: Let $j$ be the first index where Alice and Bob both succeed. As described in the protocol, $m$ is the first index where Alice succeeds and $n$ is the index such that Bob outputs the state in $B_1^n$. We have the following claim,
nodes.statement_short: Fix $j$, $m$ and $n$ as the joint-success, Alice-success and Bob-output indices.

nodes.name: Introduce the bad events
nodes.statement: Before proving Claim~\ref{claim:highprobindex}, let us define the following "bad" events.
nodes.statement_short: Define the failure events $T_1$, $T_2$, $T_3$ before bounding them.

nodes.name: Reduce index agreement to the bad events
nodes.statement: Notice that if none of above events occur, then both Alice and Bob output the same index $n=m$, and since $m$ is the first index at which Alice succeeds, $n=m=j$.
nodes.statement_short: Absent all three bad events, $n=m=j$.

nodes.name: Bound the probability that $m\neq n$
nodes.statement: We bound the probability that $m\neq n$. If $m=n$, then $m$ being the first index on which Alice succeeds, we have $m=n=j$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the analysis to bounding $\prob{m\neq n}$, since $m=n$ forces $m=n=j$.

nodes.name: Combine into the output fidelity
nodes.statement: From claims \ref{claim:successprob},\ref{claim:relativeprob} and \ref{claim:highprobindex}, the probability that Bob learns the index $j$ is atleast $1-4\ve$. Conditioned on this event, Claim \ref{claim:boboutput}, implies that the state $\rho' \in \mathcal{D}(B^j)$ that Bob outputs satisfies $\F(\rho',\rho)\geq 1-\ve$. Conditioned on the event that Bob learns the wrong index or the protocol is aborted, let the state output by Bob be $\mu$. Then Bob outputs the state $\tilde{\rho}=\alpha\rho'+(1-\alpha)\mu$, where $\alpha\geq 1-4\ve$. Using concavity of fidelity (Fact \ref{fact:fidconcave}), we have $\F(\tilde{\rho},\rho)\geq \alpha\F(\rho',\rho)+(1-\alpha)\F(\mu,\rho) \geq (1-4\ve)(1-\ve)\geq 1- 5\ve$.
nodes.statement_short: Mix the good and bad cases and use concavity of fidelity to get $\F(\tilde{\rho},\rho)\geq 1-5\ve$.

nodes.name: Account for the communication cost
nodes.statement: The communication cost of above protocol is $$\lceil\log\log\frac{1}{\ve}\rceil+\lceil c' + \log\frac{1}{\delta} + 2\log\frac{1}{\ve}\rceil\leq \lceil 3^4\frac{c+2}{\ve^4}+7\log\frac{1}{\ve} \rceil.$$ This completes the proof of theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Add the block index and hash bits to get $\lceil 3^4(c+2)/\ve^4+7\log(1/\ve)\rceil$ bits.

nodes.name: Rewrite the relative-entropy difference
nodes.statement: Following equality follows from definitions. \begin{equation*} \relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A} = \relent{\rho_{AB}}{e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}} \enspace . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Express the difference of relative entropies as a single relative entropy against a Gibbs-like operator.

nodes.name: Normalize to a state $\tau_{AB}$
nodes.statement: Define, $$Z= \Tr(e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}) \quad ; \quad \tau_{AB}=e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}/Z \enspace .$$ It holds that $Z\leq 1$ (from Fact \ref{fact:ruskai}) and hence $\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\tau_{AB}} \leq \relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}- \relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}$.
nodes.statement_short: Normalize by $Z\leq 1$ (Fact 2.10), which only decreases the relative entropy.

nodes.name: Invoke Theorem 3.1 on the new pair
nodes.statement: Bob computes the eigen-decomposition of $\tau_{AB}$ using his input. They run the protocol given by Theorem~\ref{thm:protocol} with the following setting: Alice knows a state $\rho_{AB}$, Bob knows a state $\tau_{AB}$ and both know a number ($=\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}- \relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}$) greater than $\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\tau_{AB}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bob can compute $\tau_{AB}$, so the pair $(\rho_{AB},\tau_{AB})$ can be fed to Theorem 3.1.

nodes.name: Conclude fidelity and communication
nodes.statement: They also know the error parameter $\ve>0$. By the virtue of Remark \ref{qbevremark}, at the end of the protocol, Bob obtains a state $\tilde{\rho}_{AB}$, such that $\F(\rho_{AB},\tilde{\rho}_{AB})\geq 1-5\ve$. Communication from Alice is upper bounded by $\O(\br{\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A} +1}/\epsilon^4)$.
nodes.statement_short: Remark 3.10 lets an upper bound on the relative entropy be used, giving the claimed cost.

nodes.name: Fix a Stinespring dilation
nodes.statement: Let a Stinespring representation of $\E$ be $\E(\omega) = \Tr_{A,C}\br{V (\omega \ketbra{0}_{BC})V^{\dagger}}$, where $V:\H_A \otimes \H_B \otimes \H_C \rightarrow \H_A \otimes \H_B\otimes \H_C$ is a unitary operation (Fact~\ref{stinespring}).
nodes.statement_short: Write $\E$ as a unitary $V$ on $A\otimes B\otimes C$ followed by a partial trace.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 3.11 to the dilated states
nodes.statement: Alice and Bob compute the states $V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}$ and $V\br{\sigma\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}$ , respectively. From Lemma~\ref{lem:withsideinf} and the equality $\relent{V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}}V^{\dagger}}{V\br{\sigma\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}}=\relent{\rho}{\sigma}$, there exists a protocol, in which Alice and Bob use shared entanglement and Alice sends $\O(\relent{\rho}{\sigma}-\relent{\E(\rho)}{\E(\sigma)}+1)/\ve^4 $ bits of communication to Bob, such that the state $\tilde{\rho}_{ABC}$ that Bob gets at the end of the protocol satisfies $\F(V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger},\tilde{\rho}_{ABC})\geq1-5\ve$.
nodes.statement_short: Unitary invariance of relative entropy lets Lemma 3.11 run on the dilated pair.

nodes.name: Undo the dilation
nodes.statement: Bob outputs $\tilde{\rho} = \Tr_{BC} V^{\dagger}\br{\tilde{\rho}_{ABC}} V $. From monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}), $\F(\rho, \tilde{\rho} )\geq1-5\ve$.
nodes.statement_short: Bob inverts the unitary and traces out the ancillas; fidelity cannot decrease.

nodes.name: Reduce to a fixed distribution
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be any distribution over $\X\times\Y$. We show the following, which combined with Fact~\ref{fact:yaos principle} implies the desired: \[\dqcc{, \mu^k}{\ve}{f^k}\geq\Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{, \mu}{\ve+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: By Yao's principle it suffices to prove the bound for every fixed $\mu$ and $\mu^k$.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Set up the $k$-fold protocol and its global state
nodes.statement: Let $\Q$ be a quantum one-way protocol with communication $c\cdot k$ computing $f^k$ with overall probability of success at least $1-\ve$ under distribution $\mu^k$. Let the inputs to Alice and Bob be given in registers $X_1,X_2\ldots X_k$ and $Y_1,Y_2\ldots Y_k$. For brevity, we define $X\defeq X_1,X_2\ldots X_k$ and $Y\defeq Y_1,Y_2\ldots Y_k$. Thus, the state $\sum_{xy}\mu^k(x,y)\ketbra{xy}_{XY}$ represents the joint input, where $x$ is drawn from $X$ and $y$ is drawn from $Y$. Let $\sigma_{E_A,E_B}$ be the shared entanglement between Alice and Bob where register $E_A$ is with Alice and $E_B$ with Bob. Alice applies unitary $U:\H_X\otimes \H_{E_A}\rightarrow \H_X\otimes \H_A\otimes \H_M$, where $E_A\equiv AM$, sends the message register $M$ to Bob, and then Bob applies the unitary $V: \H_Y\otimes\H_M\otimes \H_{E_B}\rightarrow \H_Y\otimes\H_{B'}\otimes\H_Z$, where $ME_B\equiv B'Z$. Since unitary operations by Alice and Bob are conditioned on their respective inputs, the unitaries $U,V$ are of the form $U=\sum_x\ketbra{x}_X\otimes U_x$ and $V=\sum_y\ketbra{y}_Y\otimes V_y$, where $U_x:\H_{E_A}\rightarrow \H_A\otimes \H_M$ and $V_y: \H_M\otimes \H_{E_B}\rightarrow \H_{B'}\otimes\H_Z$. Let the following be the global state before Alice applies her unitary: $$\theta_{XYE_AE_B} = \sum_{xy}\mu^k(x,y)\ketbra{xy}_{XY}\otimes\sigma_{E_AE_B}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Fix a protocol $\Q$ of cost $ck$ and write the pre-message global state $\theta$.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Introduce the random variables $D,U$
nodes.statement: Let $D=D_1\cdots D_k$ be a random variable uniformly distributed over $\set{0,1}^k$ and independent of the input $XY$. Define random variables $U_1,U_2\ldots U_k$ such that $U_i=X_i$ if $D_i=0$ and $U_i=Y_i$ if $D_i=1$. Let $U=U_1,U_2\ldots U_k$. Consider the state $\theta_{XYE_AE_BDU}$, with registers $D,U$ as defined above. Let $\rho_{XYAME_BDU}\defeq U\theta_{XYE_AE_BDU} U^{\dagger}$ be the state after Alice applies her unitary and sends $M$ to Bob. Since $$\condmutinf{XE_AE_B}{Y}{DU}_{\theta}=0,$$ it holds that \[\condmutinf{XAE_BM}{Y}{DU}_{\rho}=0.\] From the definition of $DU$, we thus have (below $-i$ represents the set $\{1,2\ldots i-1,i+1\ldots k\}$), \begin{equation} \condmutinf{X_{-i}AE_BM}{Y}{X_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}=\condmutinf{XAE_BM}{Y_{-i}}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the standard $D,U$ padding, which makes the message Markov-independent of the other inputs.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Bound the total conditional mutual information
nodes.statement: Since $\log\abs{M}\leq ck$ and register $E_B$ is independent of registers $XYDU$ in the state $\rho_{E_BXYDU}$, we have \begin{eqnarray*} \mutinf{XYDU}{ME_B}_{\rho}&=&\mutinf{XYDU}{E_B}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{XYDU}{M}{E_B}_{\rho}\\ &=& \condmutinf{XYDU}{M}{E_B}_{\rho} \leq 2 \log\abs{M} \leq 2ck, \end{eqnarray*} where the second last inequality is from Fact~\ref{fact:conditionalmutinf}. Consider \begin{eqnarray*} 2ck&\geq& \mutinf{XYDU}{ME_B}_{\rho}\geq \condmutinf{XY}{ME_B}{DU}_{\rho}\\ &\geq&\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{X_iY_i}{ME_B}{DU}_{\rho} \quad (\text{Fact} ~\ref{fact:chainrulemutualinf})\\ &=& \sum_{i=1}^k \condmutinf{X_iY_i}{ME_B}{D_iU_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho} \\ &=&\frac{1}{2}\br{\sum_{i=1}^k\br{\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{Y_i}{ME_B}{X_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}}}\\ &\geq&\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}. \end{eqnarray*} where the last equality is from the definition of $DU$ and the last inequality is from Fact~\ref{fact:strongsubadditivity}.
nodes.statement_short: The chain rule and strong subadditivity give $2ck\geq\frac12\sum_i\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}$.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Select a cheap coordinate $j$
nodes.statement: Hence there exists $j\in[k]$ such that \begin{equation} \condmutinf{X_j}{ME_B}{Y_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}\leq 4c. \end{equation} Furthermore, we have \begin{equation} \mutinf{X_jY_j}{D_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}= \mutinf{X_jY_j}{D_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\theta} = 0. \end{equation} since the unitary by Alice does not change the state on registers $DUXY$.
nodes.statement_short: Averaging yields a coordinate $j$ whose information cost is at most $4c$, with inputs independent of the coins.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Define the conditional states and the good set $G$
nodes.statement: For brevity, set $B\defeq ME_B$. Define the following states, which are obtained by conditioning on various classical registers: $$\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\defeq \frac{\bra{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BXYDU}\ket{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{XYDU}\ket{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}},$$ $$\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\defeq \frac{\bra{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BXDU}\ket{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{XDU}\ket{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}$$ $$\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\defeq \frac{\bra{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BYDU}\ket{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{YDU}\ket{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}$$ From~(\ref{eqn:dumarkov}), we have \[\condmutinf{Y}{B}{X_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}=0.\] which is equivalent to, using Fact \ref{fact:cqcondmut} and the fact that registers $X,Y,U,D$ are classical in $\rho_B$: $$\expec{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}\leftarrow X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}{\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}}=0.$$ This implies $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}=\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ for all $x_j,y_j,d_{-j}u_{-j}$. From~(\ref{eqn:directsummessagelength}), and Fact \ref{fact:cqcondmut}, $$\expec{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}\leftarrow X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}{\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}}\leq 4c.$$ Let $$G\defeq\set{(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j}):\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}\leq \frac{4c}{\delta}}.$$ By Markov's inequality, $$\prob{X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}\in G}\geq1-\delta. $$
nodes.statement_short: Condition on the classical registers and use Markov's inequality to get a set $G$ of probability $1-\delta$.
nodes.section: A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity

nodes.name: Build the single-copy protocol $\Q'$
nodes.statement: Now, we exhibit an entanglement-assisted one-way protocol $\Q'$ for $f$ with communication less than $c$ and distributional error $\ve$ under distribution $\mu$. \begin{mdframed} \bigskip \begin{enumerate} \item Alice and Bob share public coins according to distribution $\rho_{D_{-j}U_{-j}}$, and the shared entanglement needed to run the protocol $\P$ from Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol}. \item Alice and Bob are given the input $(x,y)\sim\mu$. They embed the input to the $j$-th coordinate $X_jY_j$. The input is independent of shared randomness, from equation (\ref{eqn:directsumpubliccoins}). \item Given input $(x_j,y_j)\equiv (x,y)$ and shared public coins $d_{-j}u_{-j}$, Alice knows the eigen-decomposition of the state $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, since $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}=\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$. Bob knows the eigen-decomposition of state $\rho_{B}^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$. \item They run the protocol in Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol} with inputs $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Alice) and $\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Bob). After communicating $\mathcal{O}(4c/\delta^9)$ bits to Bob, Bob receives a state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfying $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ if $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\in G$. \item Bob samples the distribution from $\rho_{Y_{-j}}$, since he has the registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$. This is possible from equation \ref{eqn:dumarkov}, which states that register $Y_{-j}$ is independent of registers $A,B,X$ conditioned on registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$. \item Bob applies the unitary $V$, as in the protocol $\Q$, on registers $BY\equiv E_BMY$ and then measures the register $Z$. He outputs the outcome. \end{enumerate} \end{mdframed}
nodes.statement_short: Embed the single input in coordinate $j$ and compress the message state with Theorem 3.1.

nodes.name: Account for the error and conclude
nodes.statement: From the protocol, it is clear that overall distributional error in $\Q'$ is at most $2\delta+\ve$. The error $2\delta$ occurs since the state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfies $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ and the probability that $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\notin G$ is at most $\delta$. The error $\ve$ is due to the original protocol $\Q$. Hence \[\dqcc{, \mu}{\ve+2\delta}{f}\leq \O((c+1)/\delta^9),\] which implies (changing $\delta\rightarrow \frac{\delta}{2}$) \[\dqcc{, \mu^k}{\ve}{f^k}\geq\Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{, \mu}{\ve+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: The error is at most $\ve+2\delta$; rescaling $\delta$ gives the stated direct-sum bound.

nodes.name: Set up eigen-decompositions and $K$
nodes.statement: Let eigen-decomposition of $\rho$ be $\sum_{i=1}^Na_i\ketbra{a_i}$ and of $\sigma$ be $\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i\ketbra{b_i}$. Let $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{N}}$ be an orthonormal basis for $\H$. We assume that $a_1, \ldots, a_N, b_1, \ldots b_N$ are rational numbers and let $K$ be the least common multiple of their denominators. The error due to this assumption goes to $0$ as $K \rightarrow \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the spectra and the common denominator $K$; the rationality error vanishes as $K\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Introduce the registers
nodes.statement: Introduce registers $A_1,B_1$ associated to $\H$ and registers $A_2,B_2$ associated to some Hilbert space $\H'$ with an orthonormal basis $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{K}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce registers $A_1,B_1$ on $\H$ and $A_2,B_2$ on the $K$-dimensional space.

nodes.name: Define the shared state
nodes.statement: Consider the following state shared in $A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2$. \begin{equation*} \ket{S}_{A_1B_1A_2B_2} \defeq \frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i=1}^N \ket{i,i}_{A_1B_1} \otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{K}\ket{m, m}_{A_2B_2} \right) \end{equation*} For brevity, define the registers $A\defeq A_1A_2$ and $B \defeq B_1B_2$. The protocol is described below.
nodes.statement_short: Define the maximally entangled state $\ket{S}$ and abbreviate $A=A_1A_2$, $B=B_1B_2$.

nodes.name: State the protocol
nodes.statement: \textbf{Input:} Alice is given $\rho=\sum_{i=1}^Na_i\ketbra{a_i}$. Bob is given $\sigma=\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i\ketbra{b_i}$. \bigskip \textbf{Shared resources:} Alice and Bob hold infinitely many registers $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ ($i>0$), such that $A_1^i\equiv A_1, A^i_2\equiv A_2, B_1^i\equiv B_1,B_2^i\equiv B_2$. The shared state in register $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ is $\ket{S}_{A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i}$. Let $A \equiv A_1A_2$ and $B\equiv B_1B_2$ be used as output registers. Let $i$ refer to the `index' of corresponding registers. \begin{enumerate} \item For each $i>0$, Alice performs the measurement $\set{P_A,I- P_A}$ on the registers $A^i_1A^i_2$, where \begin{equation*} P_A\defeq\sum_i\ket{a_i}_{A_1}\bra{a_i}_{A_1}\otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m}_{A_2}\bra{m}_{A_2}\right) \end{equation*} She declares \textit{success} if she obtains outcome corresponding to $P_A$. She stops once she succeeds in some register $A^j$, and swaps $A^j$ with $A$. \item For each $i>0$, Bob performs the measurement $\set{P_B,I- P_B}$ on the registers $B^i_1B^i_2$, where \begin{equation*} P_B\defeq\sum_i\ket{b_i}_{B_1}\bra{b_i}_{B_1}\otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{Kb_i}\ket{m}_{B_2}\bra{m}_{B_2}\right) \end{equation*} He declares \textit{success} if he obtains outcome corresponding to $P_B$. He stops once he succeeds in some register $B^j$, and swaps $B^j$ with $B$. \end{enumerate} \end{mdframed}
nodes.statement_short: Present the zero-communication rejection-sampling protocol.

nodes.name: Identify the joint state and its marginals
nodes.statement: At the end of above protocol, let the joint state in the register $AB$ be $\tau$. The following claim shows the first part of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Name the output joint state $\tau$ and record that its marginals give part 1 of the theorem.

nodes.name: Announce the correlation claims
nodes.statement: Following series of claims establish second part of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Announce the correlation claims.

nodes.name: Conclude the agreement probability
nodes.statement: Finally using monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}) and Claim~\ref{overlaptau} we get the second part of the theorem as follows. \[\sqrt{\Tr (E\tau)} \geq \F(\tau , \ketbra{\theta}) = \sqrt{\bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta}} \geq \left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^{3/2} . \myqedhere \]
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of fidelity plus Claim 5.4 gives $\Tr(E\tau)\geq(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}-\frac14\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2})^3$.

nodes.name: Isolate the simultaneous-success event
nodes.statement: Consider the event that Alice and Bob succeed at the same index. The resulting state in $AA_1BB_1$ is $$\frac{(P_A\otimes P_B ) \ket{S}\bra{S} (P_A\otimes P_B)}{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}},$$
nodes.statement_short: Write the post-selected state when both parties first succeed on the same copy.

nodes.name: Sum the geometric series
nodes.statement: and this event occurs with probability $$\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}^{i} \cdot \bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}= \frac{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}}{1 - \bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Sum over the number of preceding joint failures to get the event probability.

nodes.name: Discard the remaining positive terms
nodes.statement: Since the cases of Bob succeeding before Alice and Alice succeeding before Bob add positive operators to $\tau$, we get the desired.
nodes.statement_short: The other orderings only add positive operators to $\tau$, so the bound holds.

nodes.name: Apply Claim 5.3 and simplify the denominator
nodes.statement: Consider, \begin{align*} \bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} &\geq \frac{ \abs{\bra{\theta}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}}^2}{1 - \bra{S} (I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}} & \mbox{(Claim~\ref{claim:tau})}\\ & = \frac{ \abs{\bra{\theta}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}}^2}{2/N-\bra{S}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}} & \mbox{(using $\bra{S}P_A\otimes I_B\ket{S}=\bra{S}I_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}=1/N$)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Claim 5.3 and $\bra{S}P_A\otimes I_B\ket{S}=1/N$ to reduce the denominator.

nodes.name: Compute the projected vectors explicitly
nodes.statement: By direct calculation, we get $$(P_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i,j}\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\braket{b_j}{a_i}\ket{b_j}\sum_{m=1}^{K\min(a_i,b_j)}\ket{m,m} ;$$ $$\ket{\theta}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_i\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\ket{a_i}\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m,m} .$$
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate $(P_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S}$ and $\ket{\theta}$ in the eigenbases.

nodes.name: Reduce to a min-overlap expression
nodes.statement: Hence, \begin{equation} \bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} \geq \frac{\left(\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2\right)^2}{2-\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2} . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The overlap becomes a function of $\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j)\abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$.

nodes.name: Bound the min-overlap by the $\ell_1$ distance
nodes.statement: Define $R_{ij}\defeq a_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$ and $R'_{ij}\defeq b_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$. Note that both $\{R_{ij}\}$ and $\{R'_{ij}\}$ form probability distributions over $[N^2]$. Also note that $\F(R,R') = \Tr(\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma})$. Consider (using relation between fidelity and $\ell_1$ distance, Facts~\ref{fact:fidelityvstrace} and~\ref{fact:tracefidelityequi}), \begin{align} \sum_{i,j}\min(R_{ij},R'_{i,j}) & = 1 - \frac{1}{2}\onenorm{R-R'} \geq 1 - \sqrt{1-\F(R,R')^2} \nonumber \\ &= 1 - \sqrt{1-(\Tr \sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma})^2} \geq 1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2} . \end{align} Combining Equations~\eqref{eq:thetatau} and~\eqref{eq:minR} we get the desired.
nodes.statement_short: Interpret the sum as $1-\frac12\onenorm{R-R'}$ and bound it via fidelity inequalities.
